name: Pedal Steel
description: Pedal and lap steel guitar: long-ringing strings where an overlapping neighbour note bends the held one, with a shared bar vibrato and a volume-pedal swell on every note.

params.name: Swell
params.description: Fades each picked note in, as a volume pedal does, so the pick is hidden. At zero the pick is heard as it is.

params.name: Sustain
params.description: How long a held note keeps its level before it dies away. Longer rings on for many seconds, like a foot slowly opening the pedal.

params.name: Glide
params.description: How long a bend from one note to the next takes. It does nothing while Range is at zero.

params.name: Range
params.description: The widest interval that bends a held note instead of picking a new string, when the two keys overlap. At zero every note is picked.

params.name: Vibrato
params.description: Depth of the bar vibrato that every string shares. It fades in a moment after each pick, so notes start still and then sing.

params.name: Rate
params.description: How fast the bar vibrato turns. It does nothing while Vibrato is at zero.

params.name: Pick
params.description: How hard and where the string is picked: low is soft and over the neck, round and mellow; high is hard and by the bridge, bright as a bell. Applies from the next pick.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Brightness of the pickup and amplifier. Lower is dark and woolly; higher is glassy with more bite.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit, after the pedal steel and lap steel guitar as described in the project's string research notes (strings.md, sections 0, 1.3, 1.4 and 3: the legato rule, the shared bar vibrato, the volume-pedal swell, the pickup comb). Modelled: one kit plucked-string loop per string, read with an interpolator so the pitch can move; a pedal bend as a smoothed pitch change of the voice that is already sounding, with no new pick; one bar vibrato with one phase for every string; a per-note volume pedal that hides the pick and then rides the decay; a magnetic pickup as a second reading point on the string, followed by a resonant low-pass, a clean amplifier with a soft ceiling and a guitar speaker's band limits. Simplified: one polarisation per string, no stiffness, no bar or finger noise, no pitch wheel (the device interface carries none, so a slide is two overlapping keys), a fixed damping at key up and a mono output. Figures chosen here rather than measured: keys within 50 ms of a string's pick, or of the key that last bent it, count as struck together and are each picked, the pickup at 1/15 of the open string, an E9 neck played no lower than the third fret, a vibrato that waits 0.35 s after a pick and returns over half a second, a pedal ride that makes good seven tenths of the string's decay up to 12 dB, the upper partials ringing about a fifth as long as the fundamental, key-up damping of 0.6 s, and a speaker corner at 6 kHz. It uses no samples and is not a circuit model of any instrument, pickup or amplifier.
